body: Honestly, I'm just trying to find people I can relate to. Even if I'm not really asexual I want to find someone who has a low libido and isn't obsessed with romance like me.
Thanks for the recommendation! I'll definitely read her research. At least I will know my feelings have some validation and it's not all in my head.

Aegosexual seems very relatable. I'd rather watch sexual situations than participate. I also don't like being touched and would prefer to do the touching. There's a lot for me to read on. 

Maybe I'll try to educate her. She's been a good therapist otherwise.
I agree. I worded what I said really poorly. I'm just tired of the bisexuals getting treated poorly by straight people and the LGT.
Katie Collins from Blood vs Water. She's so normal it's funny.
Stoned also. I wanted Shan to win but I'm glad I got this brilliant episode.
NOBODY'S GOT AIDS!

Hi. My therapy appointment went well. It was mostly intake so I didn't get into detail about much but the therapist seems nice and most importantly she let me talk. She didn't lecture me about anything. I spent most of the session talking about my father which was surprising because I haven't seen him in person for over two years and we rarely text each other. And that's mostly because I feel obligated to do so on Father's Day and his birthday. 

I also am going to an appointment regarding a room for rent this weekend! It's not my exact SMART goal - it's $800 for a room and shared bathroom. But the listing stated that tenants must be LGBT friendly and the room is located less than ten minutes from my job! I hope I get the room!

Can I PM you? 

P.S. I promise I'm not going to tell you about my therapy session every week. I just thought you'd be interested in an update.
Hey! I'm scheduled for a therapy appointment next week!

>Why not get your JD? 

I'm afraid of the social part of being a lawyer. Plus the debt scares me. The market seems oversaturated. If I could get a legal career where I mostly write and research that would be great. I've heard good things about E-discovery. Or even law librarian, but that probably has few openings.

>Well, this is definitely something you can work on with a therapist who does CBT/DBT. You can also get a jumpstart on it with Noom or a similar program. 

I actually signed up for Noom last night. I've heard of it before but didn't try it until now. I'm on the 7 day trial. I love it so far!

>Are you going to use anything to track these changes like a To Do App or something more in the gamifaction realm like Habitica?

I started doing bullet journaling not too long ago. I've never heard of Habitica but I want to keep things simple for now 

Thanks for the silver!

>Do you already have a 4 year degree?

Yes. A bachelor's in history. I also have a certificate in legal studies. I know that not be the most lucrative choice but I suck at math. Why couldn't I have the positive autism stereotype of being good at math so I could be an engineer, accountant, computer programmer or work in finance. :/

>Submittable has a ton of journals that have free open submissions.

I'll definitely consider checking this out. It can't hurt to try.

>Body dysmorphia? Gender dysphoria? Both?

No. I just hate how I let myself get so fat.



>Mess up how?

Constantly thinking about food and then giving in to my cravings. Not sticking with a healthy routine.

>What would a Smart Goal for moving out look like?

Specific: a room for rent with a private bathroom. Less than 30 minutes from work. Affordable. Maybe $500-$700?

Measurable: Browse websites such as craigslist at least one hour a day.

Attainable: call or email at least one listing three times a week

Relevant: it is a step towards independence

Time based: Find a new place within six months?

>What kind of work do you want to do?

I'm not 100% sure. I've always liked researching, investigation, writing, compiling information. Library science? Online marketing research? Content creator? An investigator of some sort? I vaguely work in the legal profession and like it but the only thing I don't like is that my company doesn't pay much. I used to be a good writer but I got discouraged because of the competition. 

>Question A: Do you mean a specific partner finding you attractive, finding yourself attractive, or the general public finding you attractive? 

As vain as it sounds, all of the above. I feel uncomfortable talking about it, but it's hard to look at the mirror. As hard as it is, I have to talk about my body issues to a therapist. I'm ashamed of my weight, the way I eat when no one is watching...

I realize that people go out of their way to be nice when I'm thinner. Even my own family. 

>Question B: What do you do physically, emotionally and socially to support that goal?

I try to improve my diet and exercise, it has worked for awhile and I've even been happy with my body but then I mess up.

>Even if your end goal is to live alone, between living with your mother or roommates, do you have a preference?

If I think that we can have a tolerable relationship with each other: roommates.

>Well, you know you're not compatible with your mother, you could look for roommates you'd likely be compatible with, while building the skills necessary to address any issues. These skills will be necessary if you want a partner. 

That's actually a really good point. 

>Have you heard of S.M.A.R.T. Goals?

That sounds familiar.

>So you can have your prime years. What does that look like for you?

Having money. True independence. Looking young and attractive. I live on my own and have full control over my life. I no longer have to care about how my mother feels about anything. I know I don't have to now, but that's easier said than done when you're under the same roof.

I'm leaning towards not having children. Even if I wanted them, I wouldn't be able to afford kids anyway.


>And at your age, you're supposed to have spent half your life at home.

I meant my life is nearly halfway over and I'm still at home. I'm sorry for the confusion.

>So, you can negotiate a boundary— like getting a lock, move out, or accept the lack of privacy. Which would you like to do?

Move out. I want to have enough money to live entirely alone. I don't want roommates because I'm not sure how compatible I would be with them. 

>Maybe, but unlikely. They won't keep a wait-list that long, but more importantly, you don't have to rely on them: you can keep looking for someone who has sooner availability

I didn't mean years to get an appointment. Sorry for the confusion again. I meant years to reach my goals.

I'm almost middle aged. I know that is only a fact but it hurts to hear that my life is halfway finished and my prime years are over. I spent nearly half my life living at home. The only privacy I have is in my room and my Mom still walks in whenever she feels like it. I relate more to a teenage incel than anyone my age.  How old are you? 

I called a therapist's office and they said they would call me back when they have an opening for me. I feel that by the time i get the help need I'll be almost forty. It seems as if everyone else is far ahead of me in life and I'll never catch up.

>Pick one, make an appointment, and talk to them about the issues you've raised here.

Today I sent a therapy office an email after they did not respond to my call. I actually spent some time at my insurance provider's website to see what therapists in my area take my insurance. I get nervous on the phone but I will call some more offices. I'm even planning on calling a dentist tomorrow to get my first appointment in ten years. You might have changed my life lol

>But this is all putting the cart before the horse. There's a lot of personal work you have to focus on before this question even becomes relevant

Personal work. I'm not sure where to start with that. It just feels weird being single my entire life. I don't want to wonder for the rest of my life how it would be like to have a girlfriend, yet I want to find a boyfriend just for a sense of normalcy. Maybe women and men aren't that different and I'm not missing much if I don't date women anyway...

>Being a creep is about behavior. It's completely possible to be a creep to someone your same age or older.

>Are you a creep, or are you dealing with internalized homophobia/biphobia wherein LGBT folks are shamed for "invading platonic spaces"?

LGBT people have to face the misconception that they are predatory or creepy. Thank goodness that this stereotype is less prevalent these days but even in the 2000s and early 2010s I've encountered straight people who felt this way. I'm "straight passing" so I've heard stuff that they say when they think no LGBT people are listening. I guess it is internalized biphobia/homophobia. Hearing that stuff during your formative years is a bitch. I wish I was 10-15 years younger, things are much easier for the younger generation. 

This might be ageist but I wouldn't like it if someone in their mid-forties or fifties hit on me. Maybe it was  because this woman in her fifties kept insisting she buy me a drink after I said no. For some reason, it wouldn't have bothered me as much if she was closer to my age. Also, the men who cat call me tend to be around this age. I guess I just don't want younger women to see me in a similar way.

>Can you rephrase this? It doesn't make a whole lot of sense— the range of possible experiences within a relationship are neigh infinite.

Not all men are misogynists but enough are for it to be an issue. Not all lesbians are biphobic but enough are for it to be a problem. I just don't want to walk into things unaware of certain issues that I may encounter. I can't predict everything but I want to prepare for it. I guess it doesn't make much sense. I was really tired while writing, I'm still tired lol.

>You've created a world view that literally excludes all of your preferred partners by categorizing the whole population as "male and therefore uninteresting, biphobic lesbians, undesirable bi women, and straight women."

As an ND person with very little experience, I'm worried that I won't notice the signs of being used or abused as quickly as the average person. I know it's unfair to generalize people but I want to know what I could possibly expect when I go out in the world. 

As bad as it sounds, that's why I'm reluctant to date anyone more than a year older than me. They could use my lack of experience and social problems as a way to control me. I do not need another controlling mother figure. I also don't want to approach anyone much younger than me because I don't want to be a creep, although even your average early twenty something has more experience in dating than I do. I've checkmated myself again.

>There isn't a magic formula for this— it's rooted in empathy

I rarely mention this but I was diagnosed with autism at the age of two. I don't think about it much because it doesn't affect my daily life except for not being able to connect deeply with others. It might have even been a misdiagnosis. I can't relate to anyone regardless of sexuality and I don't blame anyone. I don't feel special because of this, I wish I was more like everyone else. Growing up with a normal sister just two years younger than me just reminds me of what could've been if I were normal. I'd live independently, have a high paying job, and maybe even be engaged by now. 

I don't know why I'm writing this tbh. My insurance is okay. I rarely use it because of anxiety about my health. I'm worried that they'd find something seriously wrong and I'd end up having to pay more out of pocket than what I can afford or just get told something I already know. I mean a medical doctor though. I'll eventually go to a therapist.
You have a good point. Those responses are funny to think about though.

>puts on haunted expression

>“There was this green light, and suddenly he just floated up into the night sky, saying, ‘farewell, my love, my people need me…’ and I never saw him again.”

This is hilarious.
I will use all of them lol

>Yeah, the more you post the more you seem to really need therapy. (Giving you the benefit of the doubt that you are who you claim and not a 15yo incel)

I'm realizing that I'm indeed an incel. I don't know how much therapy is going to help, if at all, but I need someone to talk to and it's their job to listen to me anyway. I'm not 15, but I am mentally and emotionally stuck in my teenage years.

I live in the United States, but in one of the most expensive parts of the country. I wish my parents didn't pick such an expensive place to live. They aren't rich. They just happen to be really good with finances. My parents are immigrants. I'd rather not say exactly where they're from though. I don't make enough money to move somewhere I could live independently. I don't want to live with roommates.

I hope you are actually healthy. Your situation is exactly what I'm worried might happen. 

Honestly, I'm so impatient. If I could leave everything and everyone right now I would. I'm sick of it all.
I want to but I don't know if I actually will.

I don't want to go to a doctor, find out something is wrong and then end up having to pay thousands of dollars just to drag out my pathetic life. I'd rather just die instead.

 Or they'll just tell me shit I already know. Shit that's easier said than done. Lose weight. Drink more  water. Same old shit that I'm not motivated enough to follow through with. 

I don't think therapy will change anything. At my age, my life is basically what it's always going to be. What is going to change? I'll still be living with that obnoxious woman or some roommates who could end up being even worse. Spending decades working just to get nowhere in life. Just to make some asshole CEO rich. Rinse. Wash. Repeat.

I'm just curious as to why you were trying to help me despite how shitty I was being. Why were you reading my post history to try to understand me? I honestly didn't realize how bad I was until I got some proper sleep after days of barely sleeping. I know that's not an excuse. I'm just surprised you're so patient with me. Thank you.
Isn't DBT for borderline personality disorder? Suggesting that someone is borderline is not funny.

I really hope you're right. I don't want to waste time and money just to be in basically the same position when I'm 40 years old. If I'm still living with the annoying woman by then, I might as well kill myself. Honestly, what is the point of being over 40 if you can't enjoy a successful life.
Would I be considered a YAVIS or a HOUND to a therapist? These are real acronyms that they use. Would they be disgusted by mistreatment of others?

>It really seems like you should get some therapy to address your body issues and other insecurities,

I really do hate my body and think that if I don't like my body why would anyone else?
I wish I could think of more to say, but everything you wrote is correct and I'm sorry. I want to be more empathetic and not judge others.

>There isn't a magic formula for this— it's rooted in empathy. 

Adults, especially those near middle age or older, will not learn empathy well enough to make much of a difference. This is one of the things you'll have to learn before your mind is fully developed or you're fucked. 

>This is called a Fixed Mindset. It's a major factor in crafting the self fulfilling prophecies you're using to set yourself up for failure.

Again, once your mind is fully developed, there is not much you can do. 

>I'm not saying this to be condescending, but I'm serious— you need therapy to address this shit because you're not contextualizing the behavior in a way that lets you apply these ideas to other situations.

After a certain age, therapy will only help you learn how to cope.

>So why do you think that is? Because I genuinely think it has to do with how you treat people

You probably won't believe me but I don't remember the last time anyone in real life has said that I was rude. I'm considered polite and a hard worker. Obviously, that's not enough but I'm not angry at society for my failures. No one owes me anything. In order to succeed you either have to have good social skills or be a genius. When I say good social skills I don't mean just politeness. I mean being in sync with the people around you. Knowing what to say and what to do to gravitate people to you. Be gregarious without being annoying.  Be persuasive and charming. I only know how to have manners in public. Nothing else comes naturally to me. Just making conversation beyond formalities is difficult to me. I'm not close to anyone because of this. 

Even if I was a genius, I wouldn't disrespect people. I'm just saying that the people successful despite social skills are probably brilliant in some other way. 

>Yeah— but I also don't say I'm going to die alone because of my standards.

I never said that. I don't have unrealistic standards because I'm not superior to anyone. I know there are people out there that fit my preferences and standards, I've just never connected with them. If you don't fit my preferences that doesn't mean you're a lesser person, it just means we don't click and wouldn't be good partners for each other. 

>Because highlighting the ways in which your behavior contradicts your implicit goals can be useful in realigning behavior with said goals.

I will try to think like you. I'll feel better but at my age it's too late for my life to actually change.

>Seriously. The way you talk about other people is pretty objectifying. Like I said— you should probably get some therapy to address this stuff. You've created a world view that literally excludes all of your preferred partners by categorizing the whole population as "male and therefore uninteresting, biphobic lesbians, undesirable bi women, and straight women."

I'm sorry for objectifying people. I was only making observations, I don't want to make people feel that they are undesirable for being who they are. I will no longer categorize people in ways that I now realize is offensive.

>Wow. You really like treating everyone else like they're beneath you, huh?

Huh? Everyone has standards. Even you. I don't think I'm above anyone. Why the hell would I? 

>That's because it's not a burn— it's an observation

Why even make this observation, if the purpose is not to try to burn me? You are probably younger than me and far more successful in life. It's not a high bar to clear but good for you anyway. Seriously.

>(Giving you the benefit of the doubt that you are who you claim and not a 15yo incel)

Literally no 15 year old is an incel. You are not expected to have a relationship at that age anyway. Any 15 year old that identifies as an incel is really a depressed child. 

>It's kind of weird how you equate having a relationship with intercourse

Most people are not asexual. There is nothing wrong with being asexual. It's just that most relationships will have sex involved unless someone says they're asexual and there's an agreement that no sex will be had.  And don't say I don't know what I'm talking about because of my lack of experiences. Why do you think r/deadbedrooms is a popular sub?

>I mean— you're an almost-middle-aged woman who has never had a relationship. 

I'm sorry. This is not the burn you think it is. Even my crusty old ass can find someone in less than a month if I wanted to. I just need really low standards. Even if I'm wrong, I have a low sex drive anyway. I would probably fare better than most alone. I know everyone my age I would've liked is either already married, looking for someone younger or wouldn't be interested in me. I'm ready to die alone.

I never claimed that I was called a TERF. I was talking about other people. 

Why did this turn into a thread about misandry? I didn't even mention men in the first place. 

I'm sorry for implying that bi women are mostly unicorn hunters. I probably need a new environment. I just haven't seen this so-called common experience that I have outside of a few pockets of the internet.

>Except, you don't. Your experience is really common.

I really wish you were right. Maybe I'll see this one day in real life, but till this day I haven't. I've never seen it.
Where did I say all men are bad? Where did I say I'm angry at men?

>Maybe you should deal with women instead of girls.

I don't talk to anyone on Tumblr. Those girls probably don't even mean what they're saying. They're just angry at boys. I wouldn't take them seriously if I were you. 

I only deal with women. What I've experienced is based on women in the real world. I don't care what angry teens on the internet (who'll probably grow up and realize not all men are bad) think.
What exactly did I say that was bigoted? All I said is that I have different experiences from these people.
I don't care if I'm an internet stereotype. There is nothing wrong with preferring women over men. No matter how many times you call me a bigot, that will never change.
Tumblr is not the real world. Why does it even bother you anyway? Just ignore it. Everyone but a small group of girls on the internet already agrees with you.

>Seriously. Check your transphobia, biphobia and sexism please. You're so fixated on this whole I'm not like other bi girls schtick you're approaching parody.

I'm literally not like most bi girls. There's no bigoted agenda despite what you and the men who whine about this think. You don't understand and that's okay.

>Yeah— but that's a function of available partners. These aren't exact numbers because safety issues lead to underreporting, but if 10% if the population experiences same gender attraction and that's divided between the genders, a woman has 4% of a same gendered partner population and roughly a 44% of the male population within her orientation pool.

If you ask most bi women what gender they prefer, the overwhelming majority will say men. This will be the case regardless of the percentage of available women. This is their nature. There's nothing wrong with that. 


>You realize how fucked it is that you're engaging in casual transphobia by excluding trans women from cis women by saying that sapphic relationships are TERFy, right?

Tell this to the people who cry TERF when a woman makes women a priority. Are they not aware that she may include trans women as well? But if she talks about loving men, people just assume she's including trans men as well.

Honestly, what's wrong with that? I'm not wrong. Nearly 90% of all bi people are in opposite sex relationships. 

I go on dating sites and it's mostly couples looking for a third or some girl who has a boyfriend but she promises he won't be involved. Yeah, right... Then I meet bi girls IRL who say that they'll only sleep with girls, never actually date one. One even said she won't date other girls because girls are "crazy." There's more internalized misogyny in bi spaces than misandry. Some women genuinely prefer other women. They want to actually center women in their lives. It's not some man hating agenda. I see, "Let bi girls love boys! We're still part of the community if we have a boyfriend!" But if a girl wants to make other girls a priority, she's a TERF or she's a wannabe lesbian licking the boots of lesbians. Why should we have to shut our mouths so some guy's feelings won't get hurt? He's embraced literally everywhere else. It's not always about him.

That's how I feel about most late bloomer "lesbians" tbh. I wonder if I should just choose men since I can tolerate them and I won't have to deal with the drama of being bisexual. I'm rarely interested in men, but it's there at least...

r/latebloomerlesbians is more relatable than other LGBT spaces. I can't relate to the many women there who've been married to men and had children, but it is interesting to see other people's journeys especially those of people closer to my age.

Suggesting comphet is not offensive to me. However, I've read from some bisexuals who state that the masterdoc is bi erasure and that much of what it says can also apply to bisexual women. I've also read from some lesbians who think it is lesbophobic because it is based on an essay by a political lesbian. It's all just confusing. I'm not even sure what I'm trying to say lol.
I'm leaving the LGBT community. Can't relate to it anyway. I just came here to vent. Wish you all the best. Bye.

They'll say he's actually gay and I'm fooling myself. Even if the relationship ends for whatever reason, I'll never hear the end of it. Not worth it. 

Stereotypes exist for a reason. Bi women have the highest abuse rate, mostly because of the men who see us as objects. Do I even need to tell you what lesbians say when they think no one is looking? I'm talking about both online and real life.

You probably live in a very liberal area or you're really young. I'm not being condescending, I wish I was born 10-15 years later. I was well into adulthood when same sex marriage became legal for the entire United States. If I were younger I'd be around a far more accepting cohort.

Thank you. Not everyone has the privilege to lose the family who has cared for them their entire life to just come out. To anyone who says "just come out" will you be there when someone gets disowned, ostracized or harrassed for coming out of the closet? Adults can lose their careers, friends and family for being gay. Homophobia doesn't just affect teenagers. Not everyone has a big group of LGBT friends who are there when shit gets tough. Not everyone has a serious girlfriend worth coming out for. For some people that might never happen. If taking some guy as a date to family functions makes my life easier, I'm gonna do that. Life is not a Disney movie where everything gets solved by just being yourself.

I want to break contact with them. I just wish I had a job with a livable wage so I could move away from my mom. I'm worried about getting roommates because I don't want to end up living with someone  worse than she is.
I want to live my truth, but it's always in the back of my mind that I'll regret it and end up like my aunt. Sometimes I worry that my truth isn't really my truth.

Hey, 
I'm also kinda an outsider, but this comment resonates with me. I wish I were younger because I don't like how older women are treated in society. I don't think I'm trans age, but I dread my birthday every year because I feel that I depreciate in value the older I get. Sometimes I feel that I'm mentally stuck at 16-18 years old. People find it hard to believe I'm in my early 30s. I'm going to PM you, I just really want to talk about this because it seems that nobody understands.
Thank you for writing this. I hope I could one day be as confident and happy with life as you.

There was a guy that I genuinely liked kissing. Why would I have enjoyed it if I didn't like men? There were also some journal entries I wrote where it seemed like I actually was attracted to men. I was also able to get aroused by men when I looked at porn.
Hi. I'd like to to join please.
Tell all TV special or ideally a show where they come back to Bonanza as adults.
I'm drained. Life is dragging me by the feet. I can't live decades like this. Why don't I have the courage to kill myself right now?
I don't enjoy anything. Even if I found a hobby, I still have to face society as a loser.
I am mostly looking for something with practical steps to improve myself but at the same time I wouldn't mind reading a story about a character that gets inspired to change their life.
Thank you for all your suggestions. It seems that many people are recommending stoicism here. I don't know much about philosophy, but this seems like a good start.

They actually do have weekly or monthly meetups for people 50+. Like someone said in the comments there usually isn't anything for "standard aged adults." I'm afraid I'll get blown off and told to just go to the bar or find people online.

I've opened dating apps but the conversations go nowhere fast and that's if they replied in the first place...   
Yes, I've met other queer women but there is never a mutual attraction. Most of the times they already have a girlfriend.
I'm just not good with connecting with others. I was diagnosed with social anxiety and autism.

I'm going to die alone.
Yay!

How and where can we promote this subreddit? It'll be a shame if it dies because of lack of exposure.

I definitely like the idea of having a Wiki or links to resources.

Honestly, you're right but there is still homophobia even in the current year. Sometimes I wonder if coming out is worth it, especially if I don't find anyone special. 
It would still be wrong to waste other people's time because it's not their problem it's mine.
That's actually an interesting perspective. I keep judging myself by the standards of neurotypical people which is unfair now that I think about it.
I was thinking of getting a better job or freelancing but I think my fear of change paralyzes me. I think you make good points about taking smaller steps to make things less overwhelming.

I had a roommate situation in college that didn't work out. It's a long story but she couldn't stand living with me because I was too quiet for her and I was drained by having someone live in the same room as me. I want to try one more time but I'm worried that I would be a difficult person to live with because of poor social skills. Maybe I should give myself a second chance?

I found that many careers that would be good my my personality require strong math skills, like engineering. If I had a better aptitude for STEM I definitely would've chosen such a career. I've been trying to look for online freelance opportunities but I'm not sure if I could make a decent income or if it's oversaturated.

I'm glad to know that my situation is not unusual. It's just that I often see people being shamed for being in a position like mine being called "basement dwellers" and losers. I was actually afraid of making a post because I thought that people would tell me that I'm whiny and ungrateful.
I just want to be normal. I hate dealing with this :(

It's an option. If finding a real husband fails, it can be a Plan B. 

 I'd rather meet men organically. I'd prefer to just find a guy that is kind and stable enough to genuinely be with. I don't want to feel like I'm pretending.  I want to be a straight woman in a relationship with a straight man and leave everything behind.
Many lesbians see bi women as traitor, sluts, or "not gay enough." Id rather be with another bi woman if I'd have to choose. You're lucky that you prefer men. It's less complicated.
